title: Your Future, Your Super annual performance test
summary: APRA published the first performance test results on 31 August 2021: 13 of 76 MySuper products failed, and products that fail twice in a row may not take new members.

instruments.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Your Future, Your Super) Act 2021

direction_rationale: Naming and barring underperforming products should push members and assets to better funds and drive exits and mergers of poor funds.
comparison: Products just failing versus just passing the benchmark

verified.notes: Date from APRA's release of the first results.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. 'alicia dates' reports 'differs': the Act commenced on 1 July 2021; the effective date used is the first published test result (31 August 2021), when failing products became known.

assessment.summary: MySuper products that fail an annual performance test must tell members, and products that fail twice may not take new members. It pushes members and assets to better funds, though benchmark-based tests encourage funds to stay close to the benchmark.

marks.reason: Naming and barring underperformers pushes members to better funds.
Repeated failure forces poor products to close or merge.
Funds are judged against set benchmarks, which discourages investing differently from them.
